reviewBasis: Independent comparison of rendered arm PNGs with the frozen source-only notes in /tmp/vector-pilot-source-review.json. This is a visual model review, not ownership certification, ground truth, or albedo acceptance.

directSVG.note: Collapses the observed three upper rows into three extreme full-height strips. It misses the discrete 9–10 visible window rhythm and its ground opening/door geometry is not proportionate to the photo.

structured.note: Retains three bays but merges each row into continuous vertical arched openings. The source has separated storeys and unequal broad-left/narrow-right apertures.

assisted.note: Closest arm: it restores a three-row, three-opening rhythm. But openings are too tall and too uniformly arched, row gaps and mixed window widths are lost, and the oversized red entrance is not source-faithful.

records.summary: Brown wall family is directionally plausible, but all arms require opening geometry correction; assistance is a starting point only.

directSVG.note: Regularizes the facade into flat window rows and omits the defining stacked central balcony/recess geometry. The large diagonal ground polygon is unsupported as facade geometry.

structured.note: Has a broadly plausible cream-over-brick banding and repeated window rows, but removes all balcony voids, rails and the observed central entrances. It also replaces observed base variation with generic openings and a foreground polygon.

assisted.note: Also omits the three stacked balcony/recess levels and creates an unsupported regular run of narrow base openings. The main floor/bay count is only superficially plausible.

records.summary: The missing balcony/recess structure is a severe failure for this facade; no arm is suitable even for a coarse game representation.

directSVG.note: Invents a narrow tower-like composition, circular ornaments and a diagonal element. It does not preserve the observed small upper opening, middle pair and distinct large arched opening.

structured.note: Reduces the source to generic rectangles and one oversized arch; visible roof/cornice structure and the two middle openings are not placed faithfully. The foliage-hidden lower storey should remain unknown, not become a definite plain base.

assisted.note: Creates overlapping upper rectangles unrelated to the photographed arrangement and an oversized generic arch. It supplies no faithful handling of the ornate roof/cornice or foliage-occluded ground.

records.summary: None preserves the small, asymmetric visible opening layout; pale material alone is insufficient.
